clips.text_zh: 又係呢條友問十年長揸邊樣。BTC定黃金真係冇標準答案，但我而家輸緊錢揀唔到，兩樣都唔想再跌🙏 算啦當儲命
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? This came up again on /biz/ tonight and anons are still split, with no clean answer.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking BTC vs gold for a 10-year hold

signal.rationale: Comparison thread with no actionable setup

clips.text_en_b2: The old question resurfaced on /biz/ tonight: if you had to lock in a single ten-year hold, would you go with Bitcoin or gold? What really tips the scales? Anons remain sharply split, and while there's no clean-cut answer, plenty of them are nursing losses on both, so neither pick feels especially safe at the moment.
clips.text_en_c1: The eternal question resurfaced on /biz/ tonight: were you compelled to hold either Bitcoin or gold exclusively for the next decade, which would merit your conviction and on what grounds? Anons remain as divided as ever, and the consensus, insofar as one exists, suggests there is no objectively correct answer. I find myself currently nursing losses on both positions, watching red ink accumulate with weary resignation. Call it preserving one's sanity at this point, because conviction requires capital I no longer possess. Bless the charts, I suppose.
clips.text_en_c2: Bitcoin versus gold, a perennial fixture on /biz/, has resurfaced once again this evening with the customary ten-year holding horizon. Anons, still nursing losses from the recent drawdown, find themselves unwilling to commit to either asset while both remain vulnerable to further depreciation. The thread's prevailing sentiment suggests a psychological retreat: holders rationalise their positions as a long-term store of value, almost a wager against the erosion of confidence itself. Yet the underlying tension persists, since neither camp can marshal decisive evidence to trump the other, and the discourse degenerates into familiar tribal posturing. No clean answer emerges.

clips.text_en_b1: Why are Dario, Sam and Musk conspiring to hold back AMERICA? 'The only control or guardrails that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the USA has that, in spades!' A /g/ anon is convinced the AI CEOs are scheming.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on Musk, Altman and Amodei vs White House AI policy

signal.rationale: Implied bullish on Musk-aligned AI narrative lifting TSLA

clips.text_en_b2: A /g/ poster is dead certain that Dario, Sam and Musk are quietly colluding to hold America back. The smoking gun? A claim that the only guardrails AI actually requires is a strong, smart, high-IQ president, and apparently the US has that in spades. Meanwhile, TSLA holders are bracing for what could turn into an expensive lesson in how fragile conviction can get.
clips.text_en_c1: Apparently Dario, Sam and Musk have been conspiring to dismantle America's competitive edge, a claim so preposterous it scarcely merits engagement, though /g/ evidently disagrees. The cited logic, that AI requires nothing more than a 'STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT,' which the United States evidently possesses 'in spades,' is the kind of reasoning that gives confidence a bad name. Whoever insisted that elevated intelligence renders one impervious to AI displacement deserves every cent of tuition I am presently paying into TSLA. Lower my cost basis in peace.
clips.text_en_c2: Why are Dario, Sam and Musk, ostensibly the architects of frontier artificial intelligence, perceived to be colluding in a manner that imperils American technological supremacy? A /g/ poster, apparently convinced that the industry's principal executives are engaged in concerted scheming, has distilled their thesis into a memorable formulation: the sole regulatory mechanism AI genuinely requires is a formidable and intellectually gifted president, which the United States, in their estimation, possesses in abundance. The accompanying scepticism is palpable, given that even ostensibly high-IQ individuals appear susceptible to the very displacement they presume to govern. TSLA holders, meanwhile, endure the spectacle in resigned silence, contemplating tuition fees yet unpaid.

clips.text_zh: AI泡沫爆咗都唔會有平GPU，全部畀人熔咗。咁我啲fe exam要既數又點算lol，靠AI續命咯🙏
clips.text_en_b1: You thought you could get cheap GPUs after the AI bubble pops? Think again, they are all getting melted down. A /g/ anon thinks the hardware will be scrapped, not dumped, so prices stay high.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on AI bubble GPUs being melted after pop

signal.rationale: Hardware shortage observation, no single trade

clips.text_en_b2: Anyone banking on cheap GPUs after the AI bubble bursts is in for a rude awakening. According to a /g/ anon, the hardware isn't going to flood the second-hand market because it's all being melted down and scrapped outright. So even if the hype collapses, prices aren't likely to come crashing down, and FE candidates relying on AI to carry them through may want a backup plan.
clips.text_en_c1: The naive assumption that a bursting AI bubble would precipitate a secondary market glut of affordable GPUs warrants considerable scrutiny, as /g/ has rightly observed. Rather than being liquidated at fire-sale prices, the hardware in question is reportedly being decommissioned and physically melted down, which would sustain elevated pricing well beyond any demand-side collapse. As for my forthcoming actuarial examinations, whose quantitative demands remain formidable, I shall continue relying upon AI as a crutch. Pray the silicon holds out long enough.
clips.text_en_c2: The presumption that an AI bubble, once it inevitably deflates, will precipitate a glut of affordable GPU hardware deserves to be challenged forthrightly. A /g/ contributor contends that the silicon underpinning the present boom will not be offloaded onto secondary markets at depressed valuations; rather, the equipment will be decommissioned, quite possibly melted down for raw material recovery, thereby ensuring that retail prices remain prohibitively elevated. The implication for downstream consumers, particularly those pursuing professional examinations requiring substantial computational resources, is stark. Should the prediction prove accurate, AI itself will continue to serve as the principal lifeline for anyone hoping to navigate the resulting scarcity.

clips.text_zh: 21 trillion美金關稅？呢條數痴線啦。Tommy問我地GI report點寫都好都唔會咁誇張wtf，到底想點🧐
clips.text_en_b1: We took in 21 trillion from tariffs? A /biz/ thread links a tweet claiming a huge tariff windfall. Anons are arguing over the real number, the timeline, and who actually pays it.

signal.rationale: Headline reaction with no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: A /biz/ thread is circulating a tweet that claims the US raked in a mind-boggling 21 trillion dollars in tariff revenue. Anons are tearing the figure apart, debating the actual timeline, the methodology, and ultimately who foots the bill. Even Tommy's GI report, infamous for stretching numbers, would have struggled to spin something quite that outrageous without raising eyebrows.
clips.text_en_c1: Twenty-one trillion dollars in tariff revenue is a figure so staggeringly divorced from fiscal plausibility that even the most charitable interpretation strains credulity. A /biz/ thread has surfaced linking a tweet that purportedly documents this windfall, and the ensuing discourse has devolved into spirited debate over the methodology, the relevant timeframe and, crucially, the identity of the party ultimately bearing the burden. Tommy has inquired how on earth our GI report ought to frame this. The question, frankly, is whether anyone intends to.
clips.text_en_c2: Twenty-one trillion dollars in tariff revenue, as a recent /biz/ thread circulating a contentious tweet suggests, strains credulity beyond reasonable measure. Anons, having scrutinised the accompanying figures with growing incredulity, find themselves unable to reconcile the headline with any plausible fiscal arithmetic, particularly since even the most generous extrapolation of recent collections falls orders of magnitude short. The episode has degenerated into a forensic exercise, with participants dissecting the timeline, the underlying methodology, and the ultimate incidence of the burden. Whatever the provenance of the claim, its propagation speaks to a broader appetite for figures that flatter rather than inform.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信睇到一定話我廢。220kg我得兩下 PR 240kg，諗住一陣call佢開gym lol
clips.text_en_b1: I went deadlifting again and did 220 kg for a double. I thought I could do more reps, I think I am just good at single reps, not higher reps. My PR is 240 kg and I have gotten stronger since, I should have tried 245 or 250.
clips.text_en_b2: Hit the gym for another deadlift session and pulled 220 kilograms for a clean double, although honestly I thought I had a few more reps in the tank. My current PR sits at 240, and since I've gotten noticeably stronger lately, I probably should have bitten the bullet and gone for 245 or 250. Fatty Sin would definitely have called that a wasted warm-up.
clips.text_en_c1: Returned to the platform this evening and managed a clean double at 220 kilograms, which is respectable, if not quite the performance I had visualised beforehand. I suspect my physiology favours maximal loads over volume work, since higher rep brackets continue to elude me despite consistent training. My current standing personal record sits at 240 kilograms, and given the progressive overload I have sustained, attempting 245 or 250 would have been the prudent course. Fat-shaming elder brother shall be informed posthaste, gym session pending.
clips.text_en_c2: Returning to the platform after an interval, I resumed deadlifting and managed a clean double at 220 kilograms, though I had anticipated additional repetitions given my present conditioning. The disparity is revealing: maximal strength, it seems, has always been my comparative advantage, whereas sustained volume work has consistently lagged. My personal record stands at 240 kilograms, set some months ago, and since then my training has compounded steadily, suggesting that an attempt at 245 or perhaps 250 would not have been unreasonable. I intend to contact my erstwhile training partner shortly, secure a gym, and demonstrate that the intervening period has not been squandered.

clips.text_zh: 講真70年代嘅動漫畫風我覺得靚過而家好多。睇完鐵之千葉又諗起Demon Slayer同Gundam 00，廢柴我連op都睇唔完lol
clips.text_en_b1: Does /a/ actually like 60s to 70s era anime and manga? The old work feels more impressive than modern Hanna-Barbera stuff, and a lot of the big mangakas of that time need more love too.
clips.text_en_b2: Does /a/ genuinely appreciate anime and manga from the sixties and seventies? There's something about that era's artwork that still holds up remarkably well against modern Hanna-Barbera-style productions, and frankly the legendary mangakas of that period deserve far more recognition. Titles like Blade of the Immortal, Demon Slayer, and Gundam 00 keep pulling people back, even if watching a full opening already feels like an achievement.
clips.text_en_c1: Does /a/ genuinely harbour affection for anime and manga originating from the sixties and seventies, or has the prevailing nostalgia curdled into uncritical hagiography? The aesthetic sensibilities of that era, exemplified by works such as Chiba's Iron and the lineage that influenced Demon Slayer and Gundam 00, possess a distinctive visual grammar that contemporary productions, with their slick Hanna-Barbera-esque polish, frequently fail to replicate. Many of the period's principal mangakas remain chronically underappreciated. This neophyte, regrettably, has yet to finish even a single opening sequence.
clips.text_en_c2: Does /a/ genuinely harbour affection for anime and manga produced between the sixties and seventies, or is the appreciation merely retrospective romanticism? The artistic sensibilities of that era, characterised by disciplined linework and an unembellished visual grammar, exert a gravitational pull that contemporary productions, however lavishly budgeted, seldom replicate. Watching Chiba LFO inevitably summons comparisons with more recent works such as Demon Slayer and Gundam 00, the latter notwithstanding its technical sophistication. The irony, of course, is that the present generation frequently forfeits patience with opening sequences, thereby declining precisely the stylistic inheritance it purports to celebrate.
